changes.explanation: The last line restores захватил: the grave equals ‘phần đất anh chiếm được từ chân đến đầu’, echoing his seizing of land; ác-sin spelled with its tone.
The red-rooster arson threat made legible (“gà trống đỏ” — đốt nhà anh) and the мир pun kept (chỗ đứng giữa làng xóm).
поспорим as a contest (thử sức); завидно as envy (ghen tị); the single Devil kept active in 2.3 (Ma quỷ nó chia rẽ họ).
разгорелось сердце / разгорелись глаза unified around rực.
сапоги consistently ủng; small naturalness fixes in 2.1, 2.8, 6.2, 6.8, 6.22 and 8.8.
Con người cần bao nhiêu đất? chosen over Một người…: the rhetorical question concerns humankind.

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.draft_rendering: con quỷ / ma quỷ / quỷ dữ
glossary.rationale: Tolstoy’s three names for the Devil are kept distinct.
Period Russian units transliterated consistently; the final three arshins are the grave’s length.
The land-seizing verb returns in the final line so that the grave is the land he finally seized.

glossary.draft_rendering: tộc trưởng (Bashkir) / ông trưởng tổng (Russian district)
glossary.rationale: The same Russian word names a Bashkir elder and a Russian rural official.

witness_decision: Selected the Russian Wikisource transcription whose stated source is Л. Н. Толстой, Собрание сочинений в 22 т., т. 10 (Москва: Художественная литература, 1982) via rvb.ru. First published in Русское богатство, 1886, no. 4; not collated.

title_review.target_title: Con người cần bao nhiêu đất?
title_review.rationale: Con người cần bao nhiêu đất? renders Tolstoy’s rhetorical question for humankind in general; the story’s last line answers it.

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: Compared the sisters, the boast, the purchases, quarrels and the move.
Compared the Bashkir country, the bargain and the night’s plans.
Compared the dream, the walk, the race against the sun and the burial.
